CausalChain: Chronic inflammation -> Activation of CAFs -> Secretion of IL-6/TGF-β -> Enhanced STAT3 signaling in cholangiocytes -> IDH mutations lead to 2-hydroxyglutarate accumulation -> Global DNA hypermethylation -> Silencing of tumor suppressors and promotion of EMT/chemoresistance
Hypothesis: In cholangiocarcinoma, CAF-derived cytokines synergize with IDH mutation-induced oncometabolic effects to reprogram the epigenetic landscape, thereby promoting chemoresistance; interrupting this CAF-cancer cell cross-talk could restore chemosensitivity.
Abstract: In cholangiocarcinoma, the interplay between the tumor microenvironment and intrinsic metabolic and epigenetic alterations appears to underlie the aggressive, chemoresistant phenotype of the disease. Chronic inflammatory signaling in the biliary tract leads to activation of cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), which secrete cytokines such as IL-6 and TGF-β. In parallel, intrinsic mutations in metabolic enzymes (e.g., IDH1/2) lead to an accumulation of oncometabolites that promote DNA hypermethylation and silencing of tumor suppressor genes. We hypothesize that the crosstalk between CAF-derived inflammatory signals and IDH mutation-driven metabolic reprogramming establishes a unique epigenetic landscape that enhances chemoresistance in cholangiocarcinoma. Disrupting this intercellular communication may reverse epigenetic modifications and improve responses to conventional therapy.
